name: Bloom and HDR
summary: Render light in a high dynamic range, map it down to the screen, and let the brightest areas glow past their edges as on a camera lens.
how: Render in a floating-point buffer; keep sky and lamps 10–100 times brighter than walls.
Blur pixels above a threshold and add them back as a glow.
Map the range to the screen with a tone curve and eye adaptation.

origin.note: Half-Life 2: Lost Coast is made to show HDR rendering.

adoptions.via: Gears of War and other HD console games use bloom across whole scenes.
HD-2D games use bloom on lamps to make pixel scenes glow.
